item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / If You Invested $100 in Bitcoin When Rockstar First Confirmed GTA 6, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today

If You Invested $100 in Bitcoin When Rockstar First Confirmed GTA 6, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today 1 min read

BTCUSD BTCUSD $100 in Bitcoin BTCUSD on the day Rockstar first confirmed GTA 6 would be worth $154.70 now, as the game rolls out worldwide this week. The Wild Ride While Fans Waited Rockstar told fans on Feb. 4, 2022, that "the next entry in the Grand Theft Auto series is well underway," back when Bitcoin traded at $41,500. That $100 bought about 0.0024 BTC, and the ride from there was rough. By Nov. 21, 2022, deep in that year’s crypto winter, Bitcoin had sunk below $16,000, shrinking the position to just $38.04. It took until Rockstar’s December 2023 trailer reveal, when the game was formally named Grand Theft Auto VI, for the position to crawl back above its starting value, hitting $101.15 as Bitcoin traded near $41,980. The real payoff came later: by Oct. 6, 2025, with Bitcoin near its then-record high above $124,000, the same $100 was worth $300.60. It has since given back more than half of that, landing at $154.70, or a 54.7% gain, as Bitcoin trades around $64,200 and GTA VI rolls out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S starting Nov. 19. Players in New Zealand, where launch day arrived first, already had access as of midnight local time, Reuters reported. That’s still enough to cover the game’s $79.99 standard edition with $74.71 left over before tax. What If You’d Waited for the Trailers Instead? The two trailer dates would have produced very different outcomes: First trailer, Dec. 4, 2023: Bitcoin traded at $41,980.10 when Rockstar revealed the game’s title. A $100 purchase then would be worth $152.93 today, just $1.77 less than buying nearly 22 months earlier when Rockstar first confirmed the game was in development. Second trailer, May 6, 2025: Bitcoin traded at $96,802.48 when that trailer dropped. A $100 purchase then would be worth only $66.32 now, leaving the buyer $13.67 short of the game’s $79.99 standard edition before tax. Disclaimer Preview Image: Shutterstock

item.content:encoded:
News / U.Today / Hyperliquid Pushes for 7 Key Tweaks Ahead of UK’s 2027 Crypto Overhaul

Hyperliquid Pushes for 7 Key Tweaks Ahead of UK’s 2027 Crypto Overhaul 1 min read

F FCA The Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority F FCA on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky. The UK's new crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027. According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection." In the letter, HPC also compared  public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote. HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe  compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them. HPC's earlier letters to regulators On Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity." On Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than new legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time. Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Intuit Stocks Fall 7.17% Two Days Before Earnings as AI Finance Tools Loom

Intuit Stocks Fall 7.17% Two Days Before Earnings as AI Finance Tools Loom Less than 1 min read

INTU Intuit INTU dropped 7.17% to $320.79 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17 as the software selloff collided with worries that AI assistants could take over personal finance tasks. Startup Fortune linked the pressure to Anthropic's Personal Finance in Claude beta, which lets users connect bank accounts and query two years of transactions. Intuit reports fiscal first-quarter results on November 19 after the close. Its own guidance calls for revenue of $4.294 billion to $4.313 billion, up 11%, and non-GAAP EPS of $2.44 to $2.48. For fiscal 2027, the company expects revenue growth of only 9% to 10% after 14% in fiscal 2026, alongside non-GAAP EPS of $22.88 to $23.12, with TurboTax revenue having grown just 7% last year.

The midpoint EPS guide puts the shares at about 13.9 times forward earnings, a multiple that already assumes slower growth. GuruFocus gives Intuit a GF Score of 81/100, combining elite profitability with badly broken momentum. Its GF Value of $840.52 puts the close about 62% below the model, a significantly undervalued reading that likely reflects years of premium multiples the market no longer grants. Thursday's report is the immediate test: a beat with steady fiscal 2027 guidance could ease disruption fears, while any cut would validate them.
